output.brief:
The main cause is the 1 April authority change, not the storm, the staff losses or the new imaging provider. Adjusters can now settle only up to $2,500. Claims of $2,500–$10,000, about half of all closures, go to the three team leads for approval. Time spent waiting for approval on those claims rose from 0.7 to 16 days. Claims under $2,500 and over $10,000 are essentially unchanged, as is the adjusters' investigation time. The team leads' trays went from about 38 items a week to over 200, and the backlog is still growing, with 455 items waiting at the end of August. The change was approved with no workload assessment. The storm surge was over by June, and the two contract hires restored adjuster numbers. I'm quite confident (about 85–90%). The evidence doesn't show whether the cap actually reduces overpayments.

What to do: don't sign for four contract adjusters or an imaging switch. Work with Internal Audit to add approval capacity for that band. For example, certify senior adjusters as second approvers, and keep a second review on every claim. Track approval wait weekly. Don't discipline the team leads. Don't scrap the control outright or make the cap permanent before the December re-test.
